summary: Built a small Python sample that demonstrates a LangChain-compatible segmentation agent with a DocumentDB aggregation tool. The sample seeds a small customers+events dataset, creates indexes, computes per-customer behavioural metrics (recency, frequency, category affinity), assigns a segment (rule-based fallback), and writes the assigned segment back to the customer profile in the sample_customer_360_08 database. A one-shot CLI demo and a small FastAPI endpoint are included. I verified dependency installation, seeding, aggregation, segmentation (write-back), and unit tests; I also inspected the live cluster (databases, indexes, documents, aggregation) via the documentdb MCP tools.
how_to_run:
1) Copy .env.example -> .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI (and optionally OPENAI_API_KEY).
2) Install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt
3) Seed the sample data (idempotent): python scripts/seed.py
4) One-shot CLI segmentation demo: python -c "import sys, os; sys.path.append(os.getcwd()); sys.argv=['', '--customer_id', 'cust_1']; from src.cli import main; main()"
   - This computes metrics for cust_1, assigns a segment (deterministic rules if no OPENAI_API_KEY), writes it to the customers collection, and prints results.
5) (Optional) Run the HTTP demo: uvicorn src.app:app --reload --port 8000 and POST {"customer_id":"cust_1"} to /segment
Notes:
- The sample reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY from environment variables. See .env.example.
- Do not commit secrets to source control.

not_verified: LLM (LangChain/OpenAI) path: Not executed/validated in this run. During an initial import attempt, langchain import triggered a pydantic compatibility error on Python 3.13; agent.py now performs lazy import and falls back to deterministic rules when an LLM is not available. The actual OpenAI/LangChain end-to-end flow was not tested because an API key was not used and langchain import may be incompatible with the system pydantic/runtime. To verify LLM behavior, set OPENAI_API_KEY and run the CLI with --use_llm; if langchain import fails due to pydantic, use Python 3.11 or pin compatible langchain/pydantic versions.
FastAPI server end-to-end HTTP demo: I did not start a long-running uvicorn server as part of automated verification, but the endpoint is provided and follows the same code path as the CLI.
Any provisioning/deployment of Azure resources (Bicep/Terraform/az): explicitly not performed per run policy; the sample uses the existing cluster via DOCUMENTDB_URI.
open_issues: LangChain / pydantic compatibility on Python 3.13: an import-time error was observed when langchain was imported at module load time. I changed the code to import langchain/OpenAI lazily and to fall back to the deterministic rules engine. Users who want to run the LLM path should either set OPENAI_API_KEY and attempt a run, or use Python 3.11 (or pin langchain/pydantic to compatible versions).
The sample writes data to the live cluster pointed to by DOCUMENTDB_URI. There is no automatic teardown in the sample; users should manually delete the sample database when finished.

If you want the LLM path validated in CI or this environment, add an OPENAI_API_KEY and confirm langchain imports successfully on the chosen Python runtime; otherwise the deterministic rules engine will be used.
